messages:
ash: noticed surge of tiny-gang pods stuck Pending in apse1 for ~45m. lots of nodes showing GPU capacity but scheduler reports nodes skipped
maria: any kube-events paste?
ash: pasted snippet:

```
Warning  FailedScheduling  42m  default-scheduler  0/120 nodes are available: 38 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 34 node(s) had insufficient resources, 48 node(s) didn't match node selectors.
```

ash: odd thing: many nodes have taint redwood/alloc-id=alloc-* with NoSchedule set ~40m ago but there are no pods for those alloc ids
kevin: that smells like stale allocation taints after preemption; our alloc-gc sometimes misses when apiserver throttles
sam: infra-bot shows alloc-gc had a TooManyRequests earlier at 1711128800
infra-bot: cleanup-job redwood/alloc-gc failed: TooManyRequests from kube-apiserver, backoff in place
maria: quick check to list nodes with alloc taints: 

kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{@.metadata.name}:{@.metadata.taints}\n{end}' | grep redwood/alloc || true

maria: result: 51 nodes with alloc taints, sample -> node-apse1-12: [{\"key\":\"redwood/alloc-id\",\"value\":\"alloc-cf12\",\"effect\":\"NoSchedule\"}]
ash: and no pods reference alloc-cf12
kevin: propose safe GC criteria: only remove redwood/alloc-* taints if node annotation redwood/alloc-heartbeat is older than X and no pod referencing the alloc exists
sam: +1, race exists if eviction just finished. suggest heartbeat < now-6m for safety
maria: will run a dry-run one-off: 

kubectl run alloc-gc-check --image=alpine --restart=Never -- sh -c "python -c '...validate nodes and print candidates'"

maria: dry-run: 51 stale alloc taints found, 15 nodes would be untainted
ash: unpack: those 15 nodes would free ~140 tiny-gang slots
kevin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) dry-run confirm 2) run GC with region lock 3) temporarily scale down warmpool by 10% to free additional capacity 4) increase alloc-heartbeat TTL in config to reduce flapping
ash: also going to PR a scheduler tweak to deweight breadcrumb score and consider alloc-heartbeat staleness when computing node preference
sam: schedule real GC at 1711130000 (in ~10m) after watch approvals; add leader-lock so only one GC per region runs
maria: infra#2341 opened with dry-run logs; fixing alloc-gc backoff to avoid apiserver throttling retries
infra-bot: deployed alloc-gc v0.3.1 -> backoff windows adjusted
kevin: running GC now with criteria: remove redwood/alloc-* taint if annotation redwood/alloc-heartbeat < now-7m and no pods match alloc-id; monitoring enabled
maria: applied patch, 15 nodes untainted
ash: scheduling improved: Pending tiny-gang count dropped 380 -> 90 in ~3m
sam: monitor preemptions; if eviction spike > 6/min, rollback GC and investigate further
kevin: eviction rate stable at 1.2/min, nvlink and net metrics normal
ash: followups: ash -> scheduler PR to reduce breadcrumb weight and add heartbeat check; maria -> harden alloc-gc (leader lock, retry jitter, stronger apiserver client); sam -> alert/dashboard for alloc-taint counts by region
maria: ETA GC hardening EOD today
ash: ETA scheduler PR tomorrow morning
sam: creating dashboard tile + pager rule for alloc-taint > 10 in region
kevin: thanks everyone, closing thread. :thumbsup:
